methodology: Train on synthetic → Validate on real → Zero data leakage
hospitalNote: Trained on 2,006 synthetic patients. Validated on 104 real patient records from a tertiary care hospital in India.

caveats.readThisFirst: These figures describe a student prototype. They are not clinical validation and this is not a medical device. Nothing here has been used on a real patient.
caveats.perClassLabelsWereWrong: Until September 2026 the Normal and Mild Pre-Eclampsia rows in this file were swapped. LabelEncoder sorts its classes alphabetically, so the encoded order is Mild/Normal/Severe, but the training script passed target_names in the order Normal/Mild/Severe and sklearn applied them positionally. The arrays were always right; the labels on them were not. Fixed in backend/ml/train_xgboost.py.
caveats.whatThatChanged: The often-quoted 'recall 0.988' belongs to the Normal class — the easy 80-record majority. Mild Pre-Eclampsia, the clinically interesting minority class, is recall 0.90 on a support of 10: nine of ten caught, one missed. A single case moves that number by ten points.
caveats.sampleSizeIsTiny: Validation n=104, from one hospital in one collection window. Per-class supports are 10, 80 and 14. No confidence intervals were computed and none of these figures should be read to three significant digits.
caveats.zeroLeakageIsOverstated: The stated methodology is 'train on synthetic, validate on real, zero leakage'. The synthetic generator's distribution parameters were hand-tuned to match the same 104 real records used for validation, so information flows from the test set into the training set through the person who wrote the generator. It is weaker than training directly on the test set, but it is not zero.
caveats.noDuplicateAudit: The synthetic training set was never checked for exact duplicate rows, and no group-aware splitting was used. On a small dataset that is the single most common source of inflated scores.
caveats.trainingAccuracyIsAWarning: trainingAccuracy of 100.0 on 2,006 synthetic rows means the model memorised a distribution it was handed, not that it learned medicine. It is reported here because it was measured, not because it is good.
caveats.syntheticTrainingData: 2,006 of the 2,110 rows the model ever saw were generated by backend/ml/generate_synthetic_data.py. They are not patients.
caveats.seeAlso: The companion preprint 'A Coin Flip Is Not a Red Light' works through why maternal-health risk figures in this range warrant scepticism, and reports the honest post-deduplication number for a comparable task. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22252076
